findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed the PIC did not wash hands before putting on gloves to prepare foods. The PIC was reminded that hands must be washed before initiating a task that involves working with food, changing gloves, after contaminating hands (ex. touching your clothes, making a sanitizer bucket, touching your phone), and upon re-entering the kitchen. Ensure that hands are always washed before donning gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Observed the following stored in the incorrect storage order:

(1) Raw beef on the top shelf of the clear double door cooler over various ready-to-eat foods (ex. bread, vegetables, sauces)

(2) Shell eggs on the middle shelf of the Coca-Cola cooler above various ready-to-eat foods (ex. vegetables, sauces).

The storage order violations were corrected during the inspection. Ensure that raw meat and shell eggs are always stored below any ready-to-eat foods to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces were not clean to sight and touch:

(1) The accumulation of debris inside of the ice machine. 

(2) The accumulation of debris on the soda machine nozzles. 

(3) The knife stored in the gap between the prep cooler and shelving (not a cleaned and sanitized surface) - CORRECTED; removed to be washed/rinsed/sanitized during the inspection.

(4) The cutting board stored behind the faucets of the dump sink - CORRECTED; moved onto the shelving during the inspection. 

(5) The soiled plastic containers holding various dry foods - CORRECTED; soiled containers discarded and the food was moved into new containers during the inspection. 

Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch. The inspector will follow-up on 11/13/2025 to ensure that the ice machine and soda nozzles have been cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed the ice scoop at the server area stored with the handle directly touching the ice. The PIC was educated about proper utensil storage. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored with the handle above the top of the food to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket available when the inspector arrived at the facility. The PIC made a sanitizer bucket testing at 150 ppm (Cl) during the inspection. Ensure there is always a sanitizer bucket available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed an accumulation of foods debris on the bottom of several coolers and freezes in the kitchen (i.e., clear double door cooler, silver freezer, large white freezer). Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the bottom of the coolers and freezers are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the facility mopped this morning and the dirty water was still in the mop bucket when the inspector arrived at the facility at 4:30 pm. The PIC dumped the mop water during the inspection. Ensure that mop water is always dumped after use.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Observed the prep cooler has an ambient air temperature between 50-60F. A probe was set between packages of green onions and was observed to be 55F. The only TCS (temperature control for safety) foods in the cooler were briskets that were just cooked (they were still very warm to the touch). The briskets were immediately moved into another functioning cooler. The only other foods in the prep cooler were vegetables that do not need to be temperature controlled and sauces that do not need to be refrigerated. These foods were allowed to remain in the prep cooler. The PIC contacted their repair personal and servicing was scheduled during the inspection. Ensure that TCS foods are not kept inside the prep cooler until it is serviced. The inspector will return on 09/26/2024 to check on the temperature of the prep cooler.

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the caulking at the triple sink and the hand sink adjacent to the mop sink is in disrepair. There is a gap between the caulking and the sinks. Ensure the caulking is replaced or repaired to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.
